title: Design System: Nous dashboard and companion

headline.purpose: The page title, one per screen.

title-lg.purpose: A group heading between card rows, and the frame name in a trace column.

figure.purpose: The value of a stat tile, in tabular figures.

figure-condensed.purpose: Readouts, durations, table totals and hour labels: Archivo at 82% width.

body-reading.purpose: A message, a tool-call reason and a reply in the trace, at most 72ch.

narrative.overview:
Two surfaces share one world. The dashboard is a nineteen-screen reading room for one expert reader; the companion is a phone-first column of cards the agent composes. Both sit on a cool chart-paper ground with white rounded cards, deep Atlantic-blue navigation, and dark ink. There is one look and no look switch.

Meaning is carried by plain words and colour. A turn is tinted with the colour of the frame the agent was in, the frame is named in a word, and a frame change is said in one sentence with its reason. A status is a word in a tinted pill. Nothing is encoded in an invented symbol.

The finish is smooth and rounded: pill controls, soft single shadows, round handles and dots. Dense data stays dense inside that finish: tables keep 13px text in rows of about 32px, numbers align in tabular figures, and the Overview keeps its timeline compact, below the cards that say what needs the reader.
keyCharacteristics: Chart-paper ground, white cards at an 18px radius with one soft shadow, Atlantic-blue rail.
One colour per cognitive frame, shown as a 7% tint and as the frame's word.
Status as a word in a tinted pill; a status colour never stands alone.
Two typefaces: Archivo for everything read, Red Hat Mono for code and tool input and output.
Dense tables and compact charts inside rounded cards.
Every colour is a token, and guard tests in the source tree pin the rules.

rules.name: The Frame Colour Rule
rules.body: The frame tokens are read by the Work trace and the Overview timeline only: as the 7% tint of a turn's frame column, as the colour of the frame's word, as the key dots, as the timeline bars, and as the short bar between two turns that runs from the old frame's colour to the new one. Screens whose data records no frame stay untinted.

rules.name: The Word With Colour Rule
rules.body: A status is never colour alone. A word says the state, and the colour agrees with it.

rules.name: The Marks And Text Rule
rules.body: A status fill is a mark; status text uses the text tone on its tint. `hexGuard.test.ts` fails a component that sets a status fill as a text colour.

rules.name: The Atlantic Action Rule
rules.body: Every filled action is Atlantic Blue. The saturated blue is left to links, focus and the question frame.

rules.name: The Separate Families Rule
rules.body: No chart series, graph node, relation or retrieval disposition colour is a frame colour or an ok, warn or error fill or text tone, and each stays a measured distance from those status tones. `tokens.test.ts` pins this, with the contrast of each colour on the surfaces it is drawn on and the distance between colours one chart draws together under normal vision, protanopia and deuteranopia.

rules.name: The Tokens Only Rule
rules.body: No colour literal, named colour or palette utility class appears in a component. `hexGuard.test.ts` enforces it, `tokenUse.test.ts` checks that every token read is declared and every token declared is read, and `oldPalette.test.ts` and `flipResidue.test.ts` keep the retired dark palette and its switch out.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Archivo and Red Hat Mono are the only faces of this world. Mono is for code, ids, and tool input and output, never for figures or labels.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: The body sets tabular figures, so numbers align wherever they stack. A number column is right-aligned.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels, headers and headings are sentence case. Labels carry no letter-spacing, and there are no tracked capitals.

rules.name: The One Timestamp Rule
rules.body: A timestamp reads "Nov 10 09:31 UTC": absolute, UTC, no seconds. Its day form is "Nov 10", a chart's hour is "Nov 10 15:00", and a heading's day is "10 November". Browser-locale dates and hand-cut date strings are refused by `timeFormat.test.ts`, which holds the `handMadeDates` check. A relative age ("2h ago") may follow the absolute time, and a turn in the trace shows its clock time alone ("09:31:07", UTC).

rules.name: The Dense Stays Dense Rule
rules.body: The shared table is 13px text in rows of about 32px. Rounding the cards does not loosen the data inside them.

rules.name: The Compact Timeline Rule
rules.body: The Overview timeline is compact and sits below the Needs you, Today so far and Health cards. It never leads the page.

rules.name: The No Shadow On Shadow Rule
rules.body: A tile or card inside a card is a flat wash at the 12px radius, never a second shadow.

rules.name: The Plain Scrim Rule
rules.body: A sheet's backdrop is a flat scrim with no blur (`browserSurfaces.test.ts`).

dos: **Do** say a state in a word and let the colour agree: "Waiting", "Clear", "4 errors".
**Do** read every colour from a token, and add a new one to the stylesheet with its contrast and distance pinned in `tokens.test.ts`.
**Do** use the white raised pill for the selected option of any switch, segmented control or filter group.
**Do** keep the page header in its one order: sub-navigation, title, then "updated" and Refresh at the right.
**Do** print a timestamp as "Nov 10 09:31 UTC", through the shared formatters.
**Do** keep tables at 13px in rows of about 32px, with numbers right-aligned in tabular figures.
**Do** set figures in condensed Archivo and tool input and output in Red Hat Mono.
**Do** put a tile or card that sits inside a card on a flat wash at the 12px radius.
**Do** make every companion control at least 44px tall, and stack list tables at phone width while wide numeric tables scroll with a fixed first column and an edge fade.
**Do** mark what is missing in words ("No frame recorded", "not yet") rather than leaving it out.
donts: **Don't** invent a symbol or use a glyph to carry meaning: no arrows, geometric shapes, dingbats or emoji in what a screen shows. `glyphs.test.ts` fails them; punctuation such as the middle dot, dashes and the ellipsis stays.
**Don't** show a status by colour alone.
**Don't** read a frame token outside the Work trace and the Overview timeline, or tint a screen whose data records no frame.
**Don't** reuse a frame colour or an ok, warn or error tone for a chart series, a graph node type, a relation or a retrieval disposition.
**Don't** fill a control with the saturated blue; filled actions are Atlantic.
**Don't** set a status fill as a text colour; use the text tone on its tint.
**Don't** write a colour literal, a named colour or a palette utility class in a component.
**Don't** bring back the look switch or a value from the retired dark palette.
**Don't** put a coloured side stripe on a callout, alert or list row.
**Don't** set labels in tracked capitals or Title Case.
**Don't** let the Overview timeline lead or dominate its page.
**Don't** format a date with the browser's locale or local-time getters, or print a cut ISO date.
**Don't** describe or restyle the companion's legacy themes as part of this world.
